title: RIC-401 Appendix E — Pattern Extraction Pipeline
subtitle: How inner-loop wins flow back into outer-loop design system. The load-bearing mechanism that keeps the design system LIVING.

nodes.label:
PATTERN EXTRACTION — the most valuable artifact update.
When a pattern works in inner loop, it gets PULLED BACK into the outer-loop design system.
Without this, the design system is dead the moment it's authored. WITH this, it grows from every shipped feature.

1. IDENTIFY
Is the pattern observable in ≥2 features?
(Single instance ≠ pattern)
Owner: HCD Expert / Architect

2. DISTILL
Name the reusable shape:
• component / token / IA pattern
• interaction primitive
• copy convention
Strip feature-specific details.

3. PROPOSE
Write proposal: pattern + 2+ examples +
rationale + suggested API.
File: PR against design system repo.
Owner: pattern's discoverer.

4. REVIEW
HCD Lead: visual + UX coherence
Architect: API + coupling
Mission Stakeholder: alignment
→ APPROVE / REVISE / REJECT

5. MERGE
• add to design system / component lib
• version-bump (e.g. DESIGN.md 2.3 → 2.4)
• update CHANGELOG.md
• tag the pattern with source feature(s)

6. NOTIFY
• broadcast to all tenants
  (FOE, RIC, Prima, SHINE)
• update onboarding docs
• mention in next sprint review

7. ADOPT
• other tenants pull the pattern
• existing features migrate over time
  (deprecation notices on old patterns)
• track adoption rate

Outer Design System
grows by ONE pattern.
Next extraction starts from
the new baseline.

Outer Design System NOW informs
the NEXT inner-loop feature
that starts from a richer baseline.
(This is the spike's spine: pattern
extraction is what makes loops nest.)

ANTI-PATTERNS (skip these and the system rots):
• extracting one-off as if it's a pattern (need ≥2 confirmed instances)
• extracting without HCD-lead review (taste collapses)
• extracting without notifying other tenants (silent fragmentation)
• extracting without adoption tracking (dead patterns clutter the system)
• not deprecating old patterns when new ones replace them (system grows forever)

CADENCE: extraction is opportunistic, not scheduled.
Trigger is the ≥2-instance signal, not the calendar.
Quarterly design system audit catches missed extractions.
